steps.content: [Background - Train Corridor]
The hands of the pocket watch have turned many times over by now. Just three hours remain until the train reaches its final destination. Time is running out for the detective.
[Background - Dining Car]
At your request, the passengers return from their compartments to the dining car one by one. Yet, none of them can sit still.

The old woman folds her napkin over and over. The young man lifts his tea that has long gone cold, only to set it back down. William simply stares out at the oppressive darkness beyond the window, as if the rails themselves might suddenly reveal the killer.
The car is filled with hushed voices. Anxiety spreads, slowly seeping into the crowd. The train continues moving forward, just as it has so far, and everyone seems to be waiting for the same thing.
[Background - Clementine's Room]

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Time is running out, Chief. Have you found your answer?
Evening has come, but the setting sun is shut out by the thick curtains. Time seems frozen within this study.
You hadn't expected Clementine to devote so much to writing these characters.
Simply sorting through their information has taken you considerable time. After all, this may very well concern a real unsolved case... You can't afford to be careless.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: ...I have a few hypotheses, but I can't confirm any of them yet.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: That's the beauty of detective novels. Anyone could be the killer, and anyone could be lying.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: A certain author from before Nightfall once left us with these words—<color=#fb9259>"Eliminate all impossibilities, and whatever remains, however improbable, must be the truth."</color>

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Unfortunately, I'm still stuck at the elimination stage.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Then, have you ruled anyone out yet?
You push the manuscript forward and rub your eyes, sore from hours of reading.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Carl from Room 101 seems to have an old grudge against the victim, and his room contains sleeping pills suspected to be the same ones found in the victim's wine. But his only connection to Redwood appears to be a business transaction.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Mrs. Jones from Room 103 is closest to the crime scene, which theoretically makes her the prime suspect. But could an elderly woman really inflict such horrific wounds?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: ...William from Room 102 certainly has the strength to deliver twelve consecutive stab wounds. But he has absolutely zero connection to Redwood.
You jot down the suspicious points about these people on the paper, attempting to piece together the stories behind them—yet all it has done is muddy the waters further.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: "The culprit must be someone who has already appeared in the story." Every character is written in great detail, but... there's no direct evidence proving any of them had a motive to kill.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Is that so? From my point of view, your deductions are already quite clear.
A chair scrapes the floor. Clementine gets up and moves to your side, examining the notes scattered across your desk with evident interest.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: ...What is it? Are you going to give me another hint?

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: No, but I am going to help you organize your thoughts a little.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: Every great detective has a trusted assistant by their side. Someone who will lend an ear when the detective is stuck, and in the end, help them to solve the case.
Clementine leans against the desk, bends down to pluck out one sheet from among the many pieces of draft paper, and carefully folds it until it becomes a small slip of paper.

She only smiles, saying nothing, and slips it into the sea of draft paper on the desk. These are the notes you jotted down earlier—information you'd categorized and organized, with the questionable parts circled.
Several sheets shift with Clementine's movements. The papers overlap, and the text you circled earlier comes into full view—

<i>
"There's a street called <color=#fb9259>Redwood Lane</color>. My child lives at street number 28."
"<color=#fb9259>Redwood</color> is a fire-resistant material, often used in construction."
"<color=#fb9259>1059</color> and <color=#fb9259>0913</color>. If they're not birthdays, then why use them as passwords?"
And at the center of it all sits the slip of paper Clementine placed down:
"Burning Redwood"

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: If you find yourself stuck, why not try approaching the problem from a different angle? You might discover something new—

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: For instance, <color=#fb9259>maybe these clues that seem like lies are actually all true?</color>
Clementine looks up in surprise, clearly not expecting you to get the answer before she can finish. You, however, remain remarkably calm.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: I see. So this is what you really wanted to tell me.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Every time I hit a wall, you'd casually drop a hint. It's almost like... you want me to uncover something. At the same time, though, you don't want me to figure it out too quickly. That's why you've been deliberately controlling the pace.

options: But I'm not a patient person.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: If you want something done right, you've got to do it yourself. Rather than waiting around for hints from my assistant, I'll handle this with my own two hands.
[Doyle's Office]

<color=#fb9259>Doyle</color>: I've gone through everything I have access to.

<color=#fb9259>Doyle</color>: There were tens of thousands of reports related to fires in Eastside in N.F. 105. Fires that broke out in buildings alone account for roughly thirty percent of those. Searching for one specific case among all these reports is like trying to find a specific match in a sea of flames.

<color=#fb9259>Doyle</color>: But, fortunately for you, after filtering with the keywords you gave me, only one case fits the criteria.

<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: ...Just as I thought. "Burning Redwood" was real.

<color=#fb9259>Doyle</color>: Well... you're right, but you're also wrong.

<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: What do you mean?

<color=#fb9259>Doyle</color>: According to the Public Security Bureau report, it was just an accident caused by electrical systems that hadn't been maintained for years. There were no casualties, so the case was closed pretty quickly.

<color=#fb9259>${PlayerName}</color>: ...Just an accident?

<color=#fb9259>Doyle</color>: That's right. At least, that's what the official documents say.

<color=#fb9259>Doyle</color>: But here's where it gets strange.

<color=#fb9259>Doyle</color>: The classification level for this "accident" is extremely high—higher than some major homicide cases, even. Normally, any sheriff could access the full file for a small fire like this. But this case? Even I don't have clearance to view everything.
A massive red warning suddenly flashes across the screen. The man scrambles to exit the system. Fortunately, he already has what he needs.

<color=#fb9259>Doyle</color>: ****, nearly set off an alarm trying to dig up intel.

<color=#fb9259>Doyle</color>: I checked those names from the novels too. Couldn't find a trace of information about 'em. They're either unregistered or aliases.

<color=#fb9259>Doyle</color>: Bottom line—I can't extract the files, but someone left an oral testimony back then. It's the only thing I can give you. Remember to delete it after you've taken a listen.

<color=#fb9259>Doyle</color>: That's everything I could find. The content isn't very... pleasant. You might want to brace yourself.
[Back to Background - Clementine's Study]
You open your terminal. At the end of the communication log is a file Doyle transmitted to you. The filename reads: <color=#fb9259>N.F.105/9/13</color>

steps.speaker: Audio File
steps.content: Yes, 28 Redwood Lane. <color=#fb9259>Redwood Orphanage</color>.

steps.speaker: Audio File
steps.content: This area used to be pretty chaotic back in the day. You'd find all kinds of people here, so a number of orphaned kids inevitably ended up on the streets. Eventually, someone with a good heart gathered them and opened a welfare home right here in the neighborhood.

steps.speaker: Audio File
steps.content: Redwood wasn't a large organization. Most of the time, it ran on donations alone. It was quite the struggle—even the staff were volunteers. Later on, it seems a benefactor started making regular donations, and things slowly got better.

steps.speaker: Audio File
steps.content: The fire that night... it started under strange circumstances. It was late, so most people were already asleep. No one was out on the streets... By the time someone noticed, the flames had already reached the rooftops.

steps.speaker: Audio File
steps.content: We wanted to help and rescue people, but the fire was too intense. Those of us who were outside couldn't get in. And the people inside... they couldn't escape. So...
The audio recording ends here.

A fire in the dead of night, spreading at an alarming rate, and a building full of children... You don't know how many could have escaped, but the casualties must have been severe. Everything you just heard contradicts the official case report.

options: Were there discrepancies in the records?

steps.content: According to Public Security Bureau records, every sheriff who worked on this case left their position within a year. They either resigned abruptly or were transferred to remote satellite towns.
Is this a coincidence? Or... did someone <color=#fb9259>cover up</color> what really happened?

The chime of the old clock in the study rings softly, a reminder that time continues to pass. All the clues you noticed but couldn't connect suddenly surge forth in your mind, everything pointing to a single, undeniable conclusion.
Across the table, the desk lamp's light reflects off her monocle, nearly blinding you. You can't make out Clementine's expression, but you do see the corner of her mouth curling upward.

steps.speaker: Clementine
steps.content: It seems you've reached a conclusion.
The sealed records, the contradictory testimonies, the sheriffs who were swiftly transferred after the incident... There's only one explanation for all these irregularities.
And she had laid out the <color=#fb9259>clues</color> before you long ago.
"But an assassination in the dead of night? That's simply not my style. I prefer something grander, more spectacular—"
"Something like... setting everything ablaze and burning it all to the ground. How does that sound?"
You've finally found the last piece of the puzzle. And as you do, all those scattered details finally come together, revealing the answer.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: "The Burning Redwood"—the fire on Redwood Lane in N.F. 105 <color=#fb9259>was no accident. It was arson.</color> As for the true culprit behind this tragedy, the one who planted the seed...

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: It was none other than the Clementine in the novel.
[Battle 6, Train Scene]
